title: AI PhD Holders From China's Top Universities Enjoy Pay Boom
key_facts: Salaries for AI PhD graduates from China's elite universities are climbing, with compensation reaching several million yuan a year (millions of US dollars).

PhD holders from top labs at Peking University and Tsinghua University who join big tech firms can earn multi-million yuan annual packages of cash, stock and options, according to one AI startup founder.
Some AI master's graduates can command daily pay in the thousands of yuan.
ByteDance, whose Beijing headquarters is less than 10 km from Peking University, is a major draw for its graduates.
Yang Ling, an assistant professor at Peking University, says a single experiment can cost several million to tens of millions of yuan, which makes high salaries worth paying.
Yang expects the AI talent shortage to ease over the next five years, and says only the very top tier will remain critical while AI coding tools take over junior programmers' tasks.
quote_evidence: Only the very top tier — those capable of delivering genuinely high-value outputs -- will remain critical. The importance of everyone else will decline,
Codex can handle the tasks these people used to perform
why_it_matters_hint: Pay for top AI researchers is high, while entry-level coding work faces pressure.
